senses.definition: comparative form of great: more great

quotes.text: The San Juan market is Mexico City's most famous deli of exotic meats, where an adventurous shopper can hunt down hard-to-find critters such as ostrich, wild boar and crocodile. Only the city zoo offers greater species diversity.
quotes.reference: 2013 July 26, Nick Miroff, “Mexico gets a taste for eating insects as chefs put bugs back on the menu”, in The Guardian Weekly, volume 189, number 7, page 32:

senses.definition: Of two (or, rarely, more than two) things: the larger in size (bigger), in value, in importance etc.
(attributive) In the names of places or geographic features:

subsenses.definition: The larger geographic or administrative area that encompasses or belongs to a place (especially if both share the same name).

quotes.text: GMRLC is a regional consortium of medium-size research libraries (17 in 1995) located in the greater Midwest.
quotes.reference: 1997, Virginia Boucher, “Interlibrary Cooperation”, in Interlibrary Loan Practices Handbook, 2nd edition, →ISBN, page 98, column 1:

subsenses.definition: (usually capitalized) Including the surrounding urban areas and conurbation (of a city or other large settlement).
examples: Greater New York includes adjacent parts of three states, as well as the City itself.

quotes.text: “Greater London!” What a vague and ill-defined term! We all known London proper, comprising of the City and Westminster, and making up one metropolis.
